summary: Two 11-story, LEED Gold office towers at 1655 & 1725 3rd St (combined ~584,000-586,208 sq ft, sources disagree on the exact figure), developed by a joint venture of Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Uber Technologies and the Golden State Warriors, designed by SHoP Architects, completed 2021, and leased in full by Uber as its San Francisco/global headquarters since January 2022 on a 20-year lease for ~4,000 employees.

milestones.text: Uber occupies both towers as its San Francisco/global headquarters, on a 20-year lease covering ~584,000-586,000 sq ft for ~4,000 employees

facts.value: Joint venture of Alexandria Real Estate Equities, Uber Technologies and the Golden State Warriors
~584,000-586,208 combined (sources disagree on the exact figure)
Uber Technologies, Inc. leases the entire office component as its San Francisco/global headquarters: 20-year lease, ~4,000 employees, 145 dedicated parking spaces

open_questions: 2026-09-23: this record's geometry was migrated off status.csv (record_id changed from the blklot '8722063' to 'mission_bay_uber_3_4') because DataSF's own Assessor Parcel dataset gives this parcel and the neighboring Chase Center arena byte-identical geometry (one shared master-condo superblock parcel). The new geometry is the union of both towers' own real OpenStreetMap building footprints (OSM ways 1410182008 and 1410183655) instead -- see the geojson's own digitization_method.

As of 2025 SEC filings, Uber still lists 1725 3rd St as its corporate HQ address, though a 2023 report said that specific building had never been fully staffed and was being marketed for sublease -- current occupancy is genuinely unclear and not resolved here.

This project's own DataSF business-registration data shows several Uber-internal registrations here (Bon Appetit @ Uber cafeteria service across multiple floors, Uber Freight Holding Corporation, a Mercedes-Benz-branded garage/showroom) not otherwise researched or added as facts in this pass.
No dedicated primary source (an Alexandria or Uber press release specifically) was found for the exact completion date of each tower individually; 2021 is used as a combined year.

2026-09-23 pass: searched for a total development or construction cost for the two towers. Press coverage only turns up financing and lease figures -- Uber's $136,000,000 payment for a 45% joint-venture stake, its $1,000,000,000 in lease payments over 20 years, and the $600,000,000 CMBS refinancing already cited above -- none of which is a stated construction or development cost, so none is recorded here.
